heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — advanced ByteDance foundation models for premium visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a dark enterprise hero with the media stack on the left and copy on the right to feel unexpected and premium. Lead with a large autoplay-muted video preview tile for Seedance 1.5 Pro, layered over a smaller Seedream 4.5 still-image tile and a compact prompt-to-output panel. Add subtle grid lines, soft orb gradients, and warm brown-orange accent glows. Keep CTA buttons solid brand accent only. This hero should communicate precision, creative momentum, and enterprise confidence while immediately showcasing both image and video generation.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a dark split-media composition
Trust uses a static logo grid instead of another card stack
Products use alternating split-panel layouts with a preview-first emphasis
Testimonials switch to a 3-card grid on a light surface after darker product blocks
Pricing becomes a comparison-led decision block to change pace before the final CTA
Final form sits in a centered card on a dark closing band to restore conversion focus
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore the models, see proof from recognizable logos, compare plans, and get started with a demo.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark authority panel with layered media collage and warm accent glow
sections.designNote: Content-first hero that answers what this is and who it is for immediately. Keep the headline explicit, the subheadline enterprise-specific, and the primary CTA as a solid accent button labeled 'Get started'. Right side should show a polished image-output tile plus a video-output tile to signal both product lines above the fold. Add 3 short value chips for speed, fidelity, and multimodal control.

Prominent logo-first trust band placed early because proof strategy is logos. Use 3–6 recognizable customer or ecosystem logos in a clean flex-wrap grid. If real logos are unavailable, replace with a restrained metric strip instead of faux brand marks. Keep it visually compact so it feels like immediate credibility, not a separate section.

Use two product blocks, not a generic feature grid. First block spotlight Seedream 4.5 with a large preview panel on one side and a concise feature list on the other; second block flips the layout for Seedance 1.5 Pro to create rhythm contrast. Because each product has 5 features, avoid static flat cards; instead use a spotlight-plus-list treatment or accordion-like feature stack anchored by a preview visual. Make the image-generation block more precision-led and the video-generation block more motion-led.

Insert a visually expressive showcase strip between product detail and proof to break the cadence. Use a dark editorial gallery with 3 compact output examples: prompt-to-image, editing/composition, and synchronized video/audio. This section should feel immersive and premium, using large thumbnails and short supporting labels rather than dense text.

Use a 3-card testimonial grid drawn from the strongest creative and production quotes. Prioritize quotes from Creative Director, Video Producer, and Art Director to match the buyer group. Keep cards clean and text-led; avoid overdecorating since the trust moment is already handled by logos. This section should validate quality, speed, and production usefulness.

Use a clear comparison-led pricing/cart section with two highlighted plan cards. Make Seedance 1.5 Pro the more visually dominant card because it has a visible price anchor and broader production impact, but keep both plans balanced. The CTA in each card must still read 'Get started' in solid accent fill. Keep the section compact and decision-oriented, not salesy.

Final conversion block on a dark closing band. Place a centered floating form card with a short reassurance line and one strong solid accent CTA labeled 'Get started'. Mobile CTA must be full-width. Keep the form minimal and friction-light because the page should end with action, not another explanation.

Do not include a marquee or news strip. The conversion architecture already prioritizes hero, trust, proof, product detail, and final CTA. Avoid adding an extra trailing logo motion band because it would dilute the end-of-page action.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium enterprise AI studio with warm branded accents, dark authority in the hero, highly readable alternating content blocks, and a logo-first trust system that feels credible for teams buying visual generation at scale.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use enterprise-style product visuals: polished AI image and video thumbnails, device mockups, prompt-to-output cards, and gallery tiles featuring generated scenes, motion frames, and audio-visual workflows. No human face hero. No cropped or black-framed media. Include a creative media gallery section with mixed video and still previews to showcase output variety.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top hero with strong left-aligned brand/logo presence, oversized headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet/value-prop list; designed as a high-contrast banner rather than a media-led split hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single hero followed by stacked content sections with clear vertical separation; content appears to move from broad positioning into detailed feature explanation, with repeated section headers and compact proof/value blocks.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content cards/blocks with minimal ornamentation, primarily text-led, lightweight borders/shadows if any, and clear hierarchy rather than decorative glassmorphism.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a prominent action in the hero and repeats within feature sections; secondary CTAs are optional and may be omitted when the page is lead-generation focused. CTA treatment favors high-contrast, concise labels and form-entry conversion.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing-first pattern; the layout is structured for lead capture and product education before any pricing consideration.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference; likely a utility or standard conversion footer if present, but not a defining pattern in this excerpt.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-forward with logo/brand media in the hero; no evidence of large editorial imagery, video panels, or media galleries in the provided markup.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature sections use stacked headline + description + capability list structure, with repeated modular blocks per product. Content is organized for progressive disclosure: overview first, then bullet-like feature evidence. Sections are suitable for tabs or accordions on responsive implementations, though not shown here.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead form block placed immediately after hero, visually separated as a conversion card. Form pattern is utility-first with multiple hidden inputs and a prominent heading, implying gated inquiry/demo capture rather than self-serve checkout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit motion pattern is evidenced in the markup; the safe reusable direction is static, conversion-focused, and low-motion.
designNotes: Prioritize clarity and lead capture over storytelling.
Keep the hero concise and bold, with one dominant message and supporting bullets.
Use modular feature blocks that can be repeated for multiple products or model variants.
Maintain strong typography hierarchy and ample whitespace to avoid visual clutter.
If adding richer interaction later, tabs or accordions would fit the content density, but the reference itself is static.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best positioned as a high-intent demo-booking landing page for solution-aware buyers evaluating advanced AI image and video generation. Because the audience is professional and enterprise-oriented, the experience should feel premium, concise, and product-led rather than promotional. Trust should be led by logos, since that is the strongest stated proof signal. The dark theme supports the premium AI category and helps the media-forward gallery and hero feel modern. A split hero is the safest conversion pattern here: message on one side, human video/media on the other, with persistent CTA access and a structured content flow that proves capabilities before asking for contact. The page should feel rich but not crowded, with clear sections, strong hierarchy, and a creative media gallery to reinforce capability without compromising readability.
